deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a pencil draft of a letter from Riemann to a 'Verehrtester Herr Ober-Medicinal-Rath'. This is almost certainly the Göttingen anatomist Jakob Henle. Henle supplied anatomical preparations to Riemann and published Riemann's posthumous fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres' in Henle and Pfeufer's Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin (1867). The fragment is reprinted in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke.

The letter's content, in order:
(1) Riemann thanks the recipient for preparations of the middle ear, which he has studied carefully. He asks to keep them until the promised afternoon visit.
(2) He states what he most wants to learn: how the malleus (hammer) is fixed in place. Specifically:
- the course of the ligamentum superius (Arnold's ligament);
- the position of the long process of the malleus relative to the walls of the fissura petrotympanica (Glaserian fissure), first written 'fissura gl[aseri]' and then struck out;
- the structures that pass through that fissure.
(3) He notes that the action of the tympanic membrane on the manubrium cannot be read off from cadaver preparations. The tension of the membrane and the pull of the m. tensor tympani change quickly after death. He therefore asks for a precise statement of which parts of the tympanic ring or the squama the short process of the malleus is most firmly attached to.
(4) He wants to explain the general course of his reasoning so that he can say clearly what information he needs. He anticipates that much of what seems evident to him will look like hypothesis to the anatomist. He hopes to convince the recipient, and hopes for his public support ('Protection'). In heavily struck passages he says it is too early to talk about how much of the work's success will be owed to the recipient's large share in it.
(5) Formal closing: 'gehorsamster College B. Riemann'.

The scientific problem served is Riemann's mechanical theory of the ossicular chain: how sound transmission works when the malleus–incus joint and the ligaments act as constraints. That is the subject of 'Mechanik des Ohres'. There are no derivations to reconstruct.

results.what: Request for anatomical details (Arnold's ligament, the long process of the malleus in the Glaserian fissure, attachment of the short process) for a mechanical theory of the middle ear; remark that post-mortem change in tympanic-membrane tension and tensor tympani pull makes cadaver preparations unreliable for studying function.
results.usually_credited_to: Hermann von Helmholtz, 'Die Mechanik der Gehörknöchelchen und des Trommelfells' (1868). Riemann's fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres' was published posthumously by Henle in 1867.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a non-mathematical draft letter belonging to Riemann's known and published work on the mechanics of the ear, done in collaboration with Henle. The letter documents that collaboration but adds no new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'wie ganz hauptsächlich mir ... Ihre Unterstützung ist' is grammatically odd. The word is likely 'unentbehrlich' (indispensable); check the image.
'mit welchen Fältchen des Paukenringes' more plausibly reads 'mit welchen Theilen des Paukenringes oder der Schuppe'.
The struck 'fissura gl' is the start of 'fissura Glaseri', replaced by 'fissura petrotympanica'.

'was ich einem Thatsachen nur durch einleuchtet' is garbled. It probably reads something like 'was einem Mathematiker von selbst einleuchtet, Ihnen bloß als Hypothese erscheinen wird'; uncertain, verify against the image.
'Auseinandersetzen' is probably 'Auseinandersetzung'; 'um ... deutlich [machen/angeben] zu können' has an inserted word.
Recipient is very likely Jakob Henle (Ober-Medicinal-Rath, Göttingen).
